intro.title: Sentence Completion — Marathon Tips
intro.subtitle: IELTS Listening — Section 2 — Question Type
intro.description: In Sentence Completion tasks, you listen to a monologue (usually a talk or announcement) and complete sentences with missing words. You must write no more than the specified number of words. The sentences follow the same order as the audio.
format: You see incomplete sentences with gaps for missing words
The word limit is stated clearly (e.g., 'NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS')
The sentences paraphrase what the speaker says — the exact words in the audio may differ from the sentence
Answers are usually nouns, adjectives, or short phrases from the audio
The questions follow the order of the audio
tips: Read all the sentences BEFORE the audio starts — predict what type of word is missing (noun? adjective? verb?)
The sentences paraphrase the audio — listen for MEANING, not exact word matches
Watch the word limit carefully — 'no more than TWO words' means 1 or 2 words only
Listen for SIGNAL WORDS that tell you the answer is coming: 'firstly', 'the most important thing is', 'make sure you'
If you miss an answer, move on immediately — the next question is coming soon
Write the EXACT words you hear from the audio — don't change the form (e.g., don't change plural to singular)
Check your spelling and grammar after the audio finishes — use the 30-second check time
Numbers and dates count as one word — '10 am' is two words, but '10am' could be written as one

practice.title: Marathon — tips for spectators
practice.instruction: Complete the sentences below. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS for each answer.

questions.before: To enjoy the day, make sure you
Stay on one side of the road to avoid
Don't arrange to meet runners near the

vocabulary.en: A person who watches an event, especially a sports event.
vocabulary.ex: "Thousands of spectators lined the streets to cheer the runners."

vocabulary.en: A long-distance running race of 42.195 km (26.2 miles).
vocabulary.ex: "The marathon starts at 9 am and the fastest runners finish in about 2 hours."

vocabulary.en: A person who runs, especially in a race.
vocabulary.ex: "Over 12,000 runners are taking part in this year's marathon."

vocabulary.en: A person who offers to do something without being paid.
vocabulary.ex: "Let the volunteers give drinks to runners — don't do it yourself."

vocabulary.en: The line at the end of a race that runners cross to finish.
vocabulary.ex: "Don't arrange to meet runners near the finish line — it's too crowded."

vocabulary.en: The roads or path that the race follows.
vocabulary.ex: "Study the route map so you know where to stand."

vocabulary.en: When roads are closed to cars during an event.
vocabulary.ex: "There will be road closures in the city centre from 7 am."

vocabulary.en: To shout encouragement to someone in a race.
vocabulary.ex: "The crowd cheered loudly as the runners passed."

vocabulary.en: To decide in advance what you are going to do.
vocabulary.ex: "To enjoy the day, make sure you plan it first."

vocabulary.en: Showing good judgement; practical and reasonable.
vocabulary.ex: "Wear sensible clothes on the day — you'll be standing for hours."

vocabulary.en: A prediction about future weather conditions.
vocabulary.ex: "Check the weather forecast the night before the marathon."

vocabulary.en: The state of the atmosphere (rain, sun, wind, etc.).
vocabulary.ex: "The weather can change quickly — bring a raincoat just in case."

vocabulary.en: Walking rather than using transport.
vocabulary.ex: "Travel on foot within the city centre — roads will be closed."

vocabulary.en: Providing physical ease and relaxation.
vocabulary.ex: "Wear comfortable shoes — you'll be on your feet all day."

vocabulary.en: To place clothing on your body.
vocabulary.ex: "Put on a warm jacket — it might be cold in the morning."

vocabulary.en: To have clothing on your body.
vocabulary.ex: "Wear sensible clothes and comfortable shoes."

vocabulary.vi: quần áo phù hợp / thực tế
vocabulary.en: Practical clothing appropriate for the situation (not fancy or uncomfortable).
vocabulary.ex: "Don't wear high heels — wear sensible clothes for standing outside."

vocabulary.en: A waterproof coat worn to protect from rain.
vocabulary.ex: "Bring a raincoat in case the weather changes."

vocabulary.en: Cream applied to skin to protect from sunburn.
vocabulary.ex: "If it's sunny, don't forget to put on sunscreen."

vocabulary.en: One piece of clothing worn on top of another.
vocabulary.ex: "Dress in layers so you can adjust if it gets warmer."

vocabulary.en: An unexpected event that causes injury or damage.
vocabulary.ex: "Stay on one side of the road to avoid accidents."

vocabulary.en: To keep away from something; to prevent something from happening.
vocabulary.ex: "Avoid crossing the road while runners are passing."

vocabulary.en: The edge or side of a road.
vocabulary.ex: "Stand on the roadside and cheer as runners go past."

vocabulary.en: Full of people; not enough space.
vocabulary.ex: "The finish line area is very crowded — find a quieter spot."

vocabulary.en: The state of being exposed to weather, risk, or an experience. In IELTS: often means contact with English or being outside in weather.
vocabulary.ex: "Long exposure to the sun can cause sunburn — wear a hat."

vocabulary.en: A fence or obstacle that prevents movement or access.
vocabulary.ex: "Don't cross the barriers — they're there for your safety."

usefulPhrases.usage: Giving strong advice or a recommendation. The words after this phrase are often the answer.
usefulPhrases.example: Make sure you plan your day before you set off.

usefulPhrases.phrase: The best way to get around is...
usefulPhrases.vi: Cách tốt nhất để di chuyển là...
usefulPhrases.usage: Recommending a method of transport. Listen for what follows.
usefulPhrases.example: The best way to get around is on foot — don't try to drive.

usefulPhrases.usage: The speaker gives a firm recommendation. The answer often follows this phrase.
usefulPhrases.example: I'd strongly recommend wearing comfortable shoes.

usefulPhrases.usage: A reminder about something important. Signals that a key detail is coming.
usefulPhrases.example: Don't forget to check the weather the night before.

usefulPhrases.usage: Telling the listener not to do something themselves — someone else will do it. The role/person that follows is often the answer.
usefulPhrases.example: Leave it to the volunteers — they'll hand out water to runners.

usefulPhrases.usage: Warning about something dangerous or inconvenient. What follows is what to stay away from.
usefulPhrases.example: Try to avoid the finish line area — it gets extremely crowded.

usefulPhrases.usage: Introduces an important fact or tip. The information after this is often tested.
usefulPhrases.example: It's worth remembering that roads will be closed from 7 am.

usefulPhrases.usage: DISTRACTOR — the speaker clarifies or corrects what they just said. The corrected version is the answer.
usefulPhrases.example: Bring warm clothes — what I mean is, dress in layers so you can adjust.

usefulPhrases.vi: Thực ra, tôi nên nói là...
usefulPhrases.usage: DISTRACTOR — the speaker corrects themselves. The second version is correct.
usefulPhrases.example: There are 10,000... actually, I should say 12,000 runners this year.

usefulPhrases.usage: Strong warning. What follows is something the listener must not do.
usefulPhrases.example: Whatever you do, don't try to cross the road while runners are passing.
